scenario: Discussing a news story with a colleague
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used in plural 'noticias' for news in general.
Used with indirect object pronouns: 'me parece' = 'it seems to me'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Has leído la noticia sobre el incendio en el periódico de hoy?
dialogue.translation: Have you read the news about the fire in today's newspaper?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, leí el artículo, aunque no entiendo bien qué ocurrió exactamente.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I read the article, although I don't really understand what exactly happened.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Según el reportaje, el suceso empezó en un almacén y afectó a varias calles cercanas.
dialogue.translation: According to the report, the incident started in a warehouse and affected several nearby streets.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Me parece que la cuestión principal es que no avisaron a tiempo a los vecinos.
dialogue.translation: I think the main issue is that they didn't warn the residents in time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Cierto, y además el tráfico se cortó durante horas, lo que complicó la situación.
dialogue.translation: True, and besides, traffic was cut off for hours, which complicated the situation.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Espero que no vuelva a ocurrir algo así, porque afecta a mucha gente.
dialogue.translation: I hope something like that doesn't happen again, because it affects many people.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, aunque al menos el artículo dice que ya están investigando las causas.
dialogue.translation: Yes, although at least the article says they are already investigating the causes.

key_phrases.translation: it seems to me that / I think that

scenario: Negotiating a minor disagreement
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Commonly used in phrases like 'de acuerdo' (okay) or 'llegar a un acuerdo' (reach an agreement).
Followed by infinitive or que + subjunctive.
Often in negative: 'no me importa' (I don't care).
May take subjunctive: 'quizá tengas razón'.
Reflexive, used with adjectives: 'ponerse nervioso'.
Used to agree with a negative statement.
Can be used for emphasis: 'yo mismo'.
In negotiation, 'punto de vista' (point of view).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No estoy de acuerdo con tu punto de vista sobre la fecha.
dialogue.translation: I don't agree with your point of view about the date.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entiendo, pero para mí la fecha actual es la mejor. Quizá podríamos cambiar algo más.
dialogue.translation: I understand, but for me the current date is the best. Maybe we could change something else.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: A mí tampoco me importa la fecha en sí, pero me importa que todos puedan venir.
dialogue.translation: I don't really care about the date itself, but I care that everyone can come.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro, la solución podría ser proponer dos opciones y que la gente vote.
dialogue.translation: Of course, the solution could be to propose two options and have people vote.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Me parece bien, pero espero que no nos pongamos nerviosos si no hay consenso.
dialogue.translation: That sounds good, but I hope we don't get nervous if there's no consensus.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No te preocupes, llegaremos a un acuerdo. ¿Te parece si lo intentamos?
dialogue.translation: Don't worry, we'll reach an agreement. What do you think if we try it?

scenario: Giving feedback on someone's work

dialogue.translation: I've read your work and I think you can improve it a lot.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Gracias, ¿qué parte no te ha gustado?
dialogue.translation: Thanks, which part didn't you like?

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.translation: Of course, in the second paragraph an important detail is missing.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: Ah, maybe I didn't explain it well because I was in a hurry.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Eso es correcto, pero no lo dejes sin revisar; el mismo problema aparece al final.
dialogue.translation: That's correct, but don't leave it without reviewing; the same problem appears at the end.

key_phrases.translation: you can improve it a lot

scenario: Explaining a problem to customer service
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Common noun for any issue, used very frequently.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, tengo un problema con el servicio de internet que recibí la semana pasada.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I have a problem with the internet service I received last week.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Buenos días, señor. ¿Puede explicarme qué avería tiene exactamente?
dialogue.translation: Good morning, sir. Can you explain to me what fault you have exactly?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: El router no funciona bien y a veces no hay conexión. He intentado revisar los cables, pero nada.
dialogue.translation: The router doesn't work well and sometimes there's no connection. I've tried to check the cables, but nothing.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entiendo. ¿Puede enviarme una foto del router para verlo?
dialogue.translation: I understand. Can you send me a photo of the router to see it?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, se la envío ahora mismo. ¿Cuánto tardará en arreglarse?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I'll send it to you right now. How long will it take to get fixed?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Normalmente, si es una avería simple, tardamos un día. Si no, podemos devolverle el dinero.
dialogue.translation: Normally, if it's a simple fault, we take one day. If not, we can return your money.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vale, pero estoy seguro de que quiero que funcione bien, no el reembolso.
dialogue.translation: Okay, but I'm sure I want it to work well, not the refund.

scenario: Talking about ambitions and career goals

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Cuál es tu meta en tu carrera?
dialogue.translation: What is your goal in your career?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quiero lograr tener éxito en mi empresa, aunque sé que no será fácil.
dialogue.translation: I want to achieve success in my company, although I know it won't be easy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y cómo piensas dedicarte a ese objetivo?
dialogue.translation: And how do you plan to dedicate yourself to that goal?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Por eso quiero formarme más, quizá con un máster en dirección.
dialogue.translation: That's why I want to train more, perhaps with a master's in management.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Crees que es posible compaginar el trabajo con los estudios?
dialogue.translation: Do you think it's possible to combine work and studies?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, aunque será duro, pero tengo claro que quiero tener éxito en mi sector.
dialogue.translation: Yes, although it will be tough, but I'm clear that I want to succeed in my sector.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¡mucho ánimo! Estoy seguro de que lograrás tu meta.
dialogue.translation: Then, good luck! I'm sure you will achieve your goal.

scenario: Discussing health habits and lifestyle
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Feminine noun, often used with 'tener' or 'cuidar'.
Commonly used in health contexts.
Refers to eating habits, not necessarily restrictive.
Physical activity.
Regular -ar verb.
Invariable in gender.
Invariable in gender.
Used here as adjective.
Describes something done regularly.
Common adverb.
Note: 'porque' is one word; 'por qué' is two words for 'why'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Últimamente me preocupa mi salud. No hago suficiente ejercicio y me siento débil.
dialogue.translation: Lately I'm worried about my health. I don't do enough exercise and I feel weak.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Por qué no pruebas a cambiar tu dieta? Comer más fruta y verdura te hará sentir más fuerte.
dialogue.translation: Why don't you try changing your diet? Eating more fruit and vegetables will make you feel stronger.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tienes razón, pero me encantan los dulces y casi todos los días como algo dulce.
dialogue.translation: You're right, but I love sweets and almost every day I eat something sweet.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No tienes que eliminarlos por completo, pero reduce su consumo. También es importante descansar bien.
dialogue.translation: You don't have to eliminate them completely, but reduce their consumption. It's also important to rest well.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Es cierto que duermo poco porque trabajo hasta tarde. Eso afecta a mi cuerpo.
dialogue.translation: It's true that I sleep little because I work late. That affects my body.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Deberías establecer una rutina habitual: duerme ocho horas y haz ejercicio por la mañana.
dialogue.translation: You should establish a usual routine: sleep eight hours and exercise in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tienes razón, voy a intentarlo. Gracias por los consejos.
dialogue.translation: You're right, I'll try. Thanks for the advice.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Cómo fue tu viaje a la montaña? ¿Llegaste bien?
dialogue.translation: How was your trip to the mountains? Did you arrive well?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, llegamos sin problema, pero el paisaje era increíble. Nos quedamos en un hotel pequeño cerca del lago.
dialogue.translation: Yes, we arrived without a problem, but the landscape was incredible. We stayed in a small hotel near the lake.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Visteis algún pueblo antiguo por allí?
dialogue.translation: Did you see any old village around there?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, un pueblo muy bonito. Tuvimos que subir una colina para verlo, y luego bajar por un sendero estrecho.
dialogue.translation: Yes, a very pretty village. We had to go up a hill to see it, and then go down a narrow path.

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.translation: Were there many people in the village?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, todavía no había llegado la temporada alta, así que estábamos tranquilos. Durante el día paseamos mucho.
dialogue.translation: No, the high season still hadn't arrived, so we were calm. During the day we walked a lot.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y cuándo volvisteis a casa?
dialogue.translation: And when did you return home?

scenario: Talking about environmental issues

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Has notado el calor extremo este verano? Es un efecto directo del cambio climático.
dialogue.translation: Have you noticed the extreme heat this summer? It is a direct effect of climate change.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, y la causa principal es que seguimos consumiendo demasiada energía de combustibles fósiles.
dialogue.translation: Yes, and the main cause is that we keep consuming too much energy from fossil fuels.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Claro, pero la gente también produce muchos residuos plásticos que terminan contaminando los océanos.
dialogue.translation: Of course, but people also produce a lot of plastic waste that ends up polluting the oceans.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Para proteger el futuro del planeta, debemos reducir nuestro consumo de plástico y energía.
dialogue.translation: To protect the future of the planet, we must reduce our consumption of plastic and energy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Totalmente de acuerdo. Una buena solución es usar transporte público o bicicleta, aunque no siempre es fácil.
dialogue.translation: Totally agree. A good solution is to use public transport or a bicycle, although it is not always easy.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Cierto. Si todos hacemos un pequeño esfuerzo, el efecto positivo será enorme.
dialogue.translation: True. If we all make a small effort, the positive effect will be enormous.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Espero que las próximas generaciones también puedan disfrutar de un planeta limpio y saludable.
dialogue.translation: I hope that future generations can also enjoy a clean and healthy planet.

key_phrases.translation: protect the future of the planet

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tuve que tomar una decisión difícil sobre mi trabajo, pero al final elegí cambiar de empresa.
dialogue.translation: I had to make a difficult decision about my job, but in the end I chose to change companies.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Y qué opciones tenías? Me parece que no era fácil decidir.
dialogue.translation: And what options did you have? It seems to me that it wasn't easy to decide.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tenía dos opciones: quedarme con el sueldo seguro o arriesgarme por un proyecto nuevo.
dialogue.translation: I had two options: stay with the secure salary or take a risk on a new project.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Y cuál fue la razón principal para cambiar? ¿El dinero o el futuro?
dialogue.translation: And what was the main reason to change? The money or the future?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: La razón fue que quería aprender cosas nuevas, aunque el dinero también contaba, pero no era el punto más importante.
dialogue.translation: The reason was that I wanted to learn new things, although money also counted, but it wasn't the most important point.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entiendo. Al final, lo que importa es estar de acuerdo con uno mismo.
dialogue.translation: I understand. In the end, what matters is being in agreement with yourself.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Exacto. Pensé mucho en cada punto, y ahora creo que fue la mejor elección.
dialogue.translation: Exactly. I thought a lot about each point, and now I believe it was the best choice.

key_phrases.translation: to agree, to be in agreement

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oye, ¿por qué has cambiado de opinión sobre el proyecto? Antes estabas muy a favor.
dialogue.translation: Hey, why have you changed your mind about the project? You were very much in favor before.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: La verdad es que acabo de leer un informe según el cual los costos son mucho más altos de lo que pensaba.
dialogue.translation: To be honest, I've just read a report according to which the costs are much higher than I thought.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y eso te hace creer que no es buena idea? Yo entiendo que es caro, pero también tiene beneficios.
dialogue.translation: And that makes you think it's not a good idea? I understand it's expensive, but it also has benefits.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero el motivo principal es que no tenemos suficiente presupuesto para arriesgarnos. Y tampoco hay garantías de éxito.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but the main reason is that we don't have enough budget to take risks. And there are no guarantees of success either.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Pero si reducimos otros gastos, podríamos hacerlo. No tienes que explicar todo tan negativo.
dialogue.translation: But if we reduce other expenses, we could do it. You don't have to explain everything so negatively.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Lo he pensado mucho, y ahora creo que es mejor invertir en algo con menos riesgo. Al final, lo importante es no perder dinero.
dialogue.translation: I've thought about it a lot, and now I think it's better to invest in something with less risk. In the end, the important thing is not to lose money.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: En mi país, es una costumbre saludar con un beso en la mejilla, pero no sé si en otros lugares se hace lo mismo.
dialogue.translation: In my country, it's a custom to greet with a kiss on the cheek, but I don't know if in other places they do the same.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aquí no se acostumbra; además, entre desconocidos, lo normal es solo dar la mano.
dialogue.translation: Here it's not customary; besides, among strangers, the normal thing is just to shake hands.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y cómo te comportas cuando viajas a otro país con diferencias tan grandes?
dialogue.translation: And how do you behave when you travel to another country with such big differences?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Creo que lo importante es respetar las costumbres locales, aunque no las entiendas del todo.
dialogue.translation: I think the important thing is to respect local customs, even if you don't fully understand them.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, pero quizás en algunas situaciones es difícil saber qué se permite y qué no.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but maybe in some situations it's hard to know what is allowed and what isn't.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Según mi experiencia, lo mejor es observar y preguntar si tienes dudas.
dialogue.translation: According to my experience, the best thing is to observe and ask if you have doubts.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tienes razón, así se evitan malentendidos y se aprende mucho de cada cultura.
dialogue.translation: You're right, that way misunderstandings are avoided and you learn a lot from each culture.

key_phrases.translation: the important thing is to respect

scenario: Discussing technology in daily life

dialogue.translation: Lately I use my phone a lot to search for information, but sometimes I forget to update the apps.

dialogue.translation: Yes, it's important to update them to improve security and also the speed of the device.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: I usually use a USB cable, but you can also do it wirelessly if both devices allow it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Crees que la seguridad de mis datos está en peligro si uso wifi pública?
dialogue.translation: Do you think the security of my data is at risk if I use public wifi?

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: It could be, that's why it's better not to use apps that have personal information on those networks.

dialogue.translation: You're right, and don't forget to share your security tips with me whenever you want.

dialogue.text: Propongo que hagamos una encuesta rápida para ver qué opina el equipo. Así que, quizá podamos decidir mejor.
dialogue.translation: I propose that we do a quick survey to see what the team thinks. So, perhaps we can decide better.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfecto, consideraremos esa opción. Sin embargo, debemos recordar que el asunto principal es el presupuesto, no las encuestas.
dialogue.translation: Perfect, we will consider that option. However, we must remember that the main matter is the budget, not surveys.

scenario: Describing a person's character in depth
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used to describe a person's nature.
Describes someone who tells the truth.
Can have positive or negative connotation depending on context.
Describes someone who can wait calmly.
Easily affected by emotions; not the same as 'sensible' in English.
Commonly used for emotional support.
Often used with 'en' (confiar en alguien).
Used with infinitive: 'suele ser' = 'is usually'.
Used to express negation, often with 'no' or alone.
Can refer to physical or mental strength.
Used to introduce a contrasting idea.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Cómo describirías el carácter de tu hermana?
dialogue.translation: How would you describe your sister's character?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Es muy sincera y siempre dice lo que piensa, aunque a veces resulta demasiado directa.
dialogue.translation: She is very sincere and always says what she thinks, although sometimes she comes across as too direct.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y es orgullosa?
dialogue.translation: And is she proud?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, bastante. Pero también es muy paciente y sabe escuchar cuando alguien necesita apoyo.
dialogue.translation: Yes, quite. But she is also very patient and knows how to listen when someone needs support.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Suena como una persona sensible, ¿no?
dialogue.translation: She sounds like a sensitive person, doesn't she?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, aunque no lo demuestra mucho. Pero puedes confiar en ella; nunca te va a fallar.
dialogue.translation: Yes, although she doesn't show it much. But you can trust her; she will never let you down.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Parece una persona fuerte. ¿Suele ser así con todos?
dialogue.translation: She seems like a strong person. Is she usually like that with everyone?

scenario: Talking about education and learning
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Common verb for acquiring knowledge or skills.
Used with direct and indirect objects: enseñar algo a alguien.
Often used in plural 'estudios' for formal education.
Abstract noun, often uncountable.
Can refer to a course or a school year.
Refers to practical application or exercise.
Regular -ar verb.
Used for language levels, etc.
Often used with 'hacer' – hacer un esfuerzo.
Opposite: difícil.
Used to express agreement with a negative statement.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Estoy haciendo un curso de español para mejorar mi nivel.
dialogue.translation: I'm taking a Spanish course to improve my level.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Y cómo lo llevas? ¿Es fácil o tienes que hacer mucho esfuerzo?
dialogue.translation: And how is it going? Is it easy or do you have to make a lot of effort?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No es nada fácil, pero cada día aprendo algo nuevo. Lo que más me gusta es la práctica oral.
dialogue.translation: It's not easy at all, but every day I learn something new. What I like most is oral practice.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Eso es bueno. A mí me encanta aprender vocabulario, pero tampoco tengo tiempo para estudiar mucho.
dialogue.translation: That's good. I love learning vocabulary, but I also don't have time to study much.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Puedes aprovechar los fines de semana. Además, el conocimiento que ganas con el estudio siempre te ayuda.
dialogue.translation: You can take advantage of the weekends. Besides, the knowledge you gain from studying always helps you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Tienes razón. ¿Y quién te enseña en ese curso?
dialogue.translation: You're right. And who teaches you in that course?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Una profesora muy buena. Ella insiste en que la práctica diaria es clave para aprender bien.
dialogue.translation: A very good teacher. She insists that daily practice is key to learning well.

scenario: Discussing a problem and offering solutions
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Masculine noun, often used with 'tener' or 'resolver'.
Feminine noun, commonly used with 'buscar' or 'encontrar'.
Regular -ar verb; often used with direct object.
Regular -ar verb; used with infinitive or noun.
Used with indirect object pronouns: 'me parece', 'te parece'.
Feminine noun; also used in expressions like 'darse cuenta' (to realize).
Regular -ar verb; used with 'por' for what you pay for.
Feminine noun; 'tener razón' = to be right.
Invariable in gender; used with 'es posible que' + subjunctive.
Variant of 'quizás'; often followed by subjunctive.
Don't confuse with 'por qué' (why).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tengo un problema con la cuenta del teléfono, porque me han cobrado de más este mes.
dialogue.translation: I have a problem with the phone bill, because they've charged me extra this month.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Qué te parece? Quizá puedas llamar a la compañía y pedir una solución.
dialogue.translation: What do you think? Maybe you can call the company and ask for a solution.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ya lo intenté, pero necesitaría pagar una tasa para revisar el contrato, y no quiero cambiar de plan.
dialogue.translation: I already tried, but I would need to pay a fee to review the contract, and I don't want to change my plan.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Tienes razón? Quizá no sea posible evitar el cargo, pero podrías pedir una factura detallada.
dialogue.translation: Are you right? Maybe it's not possible to avoid the charge, but you could ask for a detailed invoice.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, tienes razón, pero me parece injusto porque no usé más datos este mes.
dialogue.translation: Yes, you're right, but it seems unfair to me because I didn't use more data this month.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quizá la solución sea presentar una reclamación formal. Así podrías cambiar el cargo sin pagar nada.
dialogue.translation: Maybe the solution is to file a formal complaint. That way you could change the charge without paying anything.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buena idea, lo intentaré. Gracias por la ayuda, porque ya no sabía qué hacer.
dialogue.translation: Good idea, I'll try it. Thanks for the help, because I didn't know what to do anymore.

scenario: Comparing two options for a trip
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Common alternative to 'escoger'

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Estoy comparando dos opciones para el viaje a Madrid. Una es más barata pero tarda más.
dialogue.translation: I'm comparing two options for the trip to Madrid. One is cheaper but takes longer.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Cuál es más cara? ¿La que es directa o la que tiene escala?
dialogue.translation: Which one is more expensive? The direct one or the one with a stopover?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: La directa es más cara, pero además sale de un aeropuerto que está cerca de mi casa.
dialogue.translation: The direct one is more expensive, but it also departs from an airport that is near my house.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Aunque la otra opción es más lejos, quizá te conviene por el precio.
dialogue.translation: Although the other option is farther, maybe it's better for you because of the price.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, pero prefiero pagar un poco más y llegar antes.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I prefer to pay a bit more and arrive earlier.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entonces, ¿vas a elegir la directa?
dialogue.translation: So, are you going to choose the direct one?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, aunque sea más cara, la comodidad vale la pena.
dialogue.translation: Yes, even though it's more expensive, the comfort is worth it.

scenario: Talking about social media habits
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Used to talk about how often something happens.
Commonly used to cite sources or opinions.
Often used in plural: 'noticias'.
Common in contexts of checking social media.
Can mean 'sure' (certain) or 'safe' (secure).
Essential for social media contexts.
Used to refer to a specific time.
Distinct from 'vez' (occasion) and 'hora' (hour).
Commonly used with 'tiempo' – 'perder el tiempo' (waste time).
Refers to phone, computer, or TV screen.
Used to talk about evidence or proof of something.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Con qué frecuencia revisas tus redes sociales?
dialogue.translation: How often do you check your social media?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Según mi rutina, las reviso cada pocos minutos. Siempre quiero comprobar si hay alguna noticia nueva.
dialogue.translation: According to my routine, I check them every few minutes. I always want to check if there is any new news.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿No te preocupa perder el tiempo? Yo intento no estar tan pendiente de la pantalla.
dialogue.translation: Aren't you worried about wasting time? I try not to be so glued to the screen.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: A veces siento que pierdo el tiempo, pero también es un buen momento para compartir cosas con mis amigos.
dialogue.translation: Sometimes I feel like I waste time, but it's also a good moment to share things with my friends.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Es cierto, pero ¿estás seguro de que no te afecta? Yo he visto pruebas de que demasiado uso es malo.
dialogue.translation: That's true, but are you sure it doesn't affect you? I've seen proof that too much use is bad.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No tengo pruebas claras, pero sé que debo controlar el tiempo. Quizá reduzca el uso de las redes.
dialogue.translation: I don't have clear proof, but I know I should control my time. Maybe I'll reduce my use of social media.

key_phrases.translation: to be glued to / keep an eye on

scenario: Giving a short presentation at work
frequency_note: words ranked ~700–1500 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Used for introducing a topic or presenting information.
Plural noun; commonly used in professional contexts.
Used as a discourse connector to introduce a consequence or next step.
Followed by a noun or pronoun, not a verb.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buenos días a todos. Voy a presentar un resumen breve del proyecto.
dialogue.translation: Good morning everyone. I am going to present a brief summary of the project.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perfecto. ¿Cuál es el objetivo principal de esta presentación?
dialogue.translation: Perfect. What is the main objective of this presentation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: El objetivo es mostrar los resultados del último trimestre, según los datos que recopilamos.
dialogue.translation: The objective is to show the results of the last quarter, according to the data we collected.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entiendo. ¿Va a incluir las cifras de ventas también?
dialogue.translation: I understand. Are you going to include the sales figures as well?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, las incluyo en la sección de ventas. Entonces, pasaré a las proyecciones para el próximo año.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I include them in the sales section. Then, I will move on to the projections for next year.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Muy bien. ¿Y cómo piensa concluir la presentación?
dialogue.translation: Very well. And how do you plan to conclude the presentation?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Finalmente, haré un resumen de los puntos clave y abriré un turno de preguntas.
dialogue.translation: Finally, I will do a summary of the key points and open a Q&A session.

key_phrases.translation: I will move on to the projections
I will open a Q&A session

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Sigues algún deporte o tienes alguna afición que te guste seguir?
dialogue.translation: Do you follow any sport or have a hobby you like to keep up with?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, me encanta el fútbol. Mi equipo favorito es el Real Madrid, y sigo cada partido de la temporada.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I love football. My favorite team is Real Madrid, and I follow every match of the season.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Quién es tu jugador preferido? ¿Y qué piensas del entrenador actual?
dialogue.translation: Who is your preferred player? And what do you think of the current coach?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Mi jugador preferido es Vinícius, pero creo que el entrenador no está haciendo un buen trabajo. Este año hemos perdido muchos partidos importantes.
dialogue.translation: My preferred player is Vinícius, but I think the coach isn't doing a good job. This year we have lost many important matches.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entiendo. Pero todavía pueden ganar el campeonato, ¿no?
dialogue.translation: I understand. But they can still win the championship, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Espero que sí, pero será difícil. Sin embargo, lo bueno es que siempre seguimos al equipo, aunque pierda.
dialogue.translation: I hope so, but it will be difficult. However, the good thing is that we always follow the team, even if they lose.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¡Así se hace! Al final, lo importante es disfrutar de la afición y de cada partido.
dialogue.translation: That's the way! In the end, what matters is enjoying the hobby and each match.
